text: Negligence requires duty, breach, causation, and damages.
A contract may be terminated after a material breach.
A breach of duty occurs when a person fails to meet the required standard of care.
Strict liability may apply even when the defendant did not act negligently.
Damages are a monetary remedy awarded for losses caused by wrongful conduct.
A minor contractual violation does not necessarily justify ending the agreement.
Contracts can also end when both parties mutually agree to cancel their obligations.
A fiduciary duty requires a person to act loyally in the interests of another.
The standard of care describes the level of caution expected from a reasonable person.
